title: Add a class
d: Create a class: name, days of the week, and times.
dec: Days are a multi-select chip row using the design system's selection magenta.
Minimum viable field set — anything not needed to take a register is deferred.
a: Times are the same on every selected day; per-day variation is not supported.
p: Per-day times and term dates are proposed for a later release.

title: Add expense
d: Records an outgoing amount against the month.
dec: Kept to amount, category and date — enough for a monthly picture, not a full accounting tool.
a: Expense categories are a fixed list.
p: Attaching a photo of a receipt is proposed.

title: Add staff
d: Adds a practitioner to the preschool.
dec: Minimal field set; the practitioner completes their own profile on first sign-in.
a: Invitation is by phone number, matching the onboarding model.
p: Bulk invite is proposed.

title: Attendance saved
d: Confirmation after submitting a register, including the sync state of the record.
dec: The confirmation states where the data is ('saved on your phone' vs synced), because offline is the normal case.
Uses the design system Success alert rather than a transient toast, so the state is still visible after a scroll.
a: Saving is always allowed offline; the queue reconciles later.
p: An undo window immediately after save is proposed.

title: Take attendance
d: The register for one class on one day. Every child defaults to present; the practitioner taps only the exceptions.
dec: Default-present, tap-absent — the fastest path for the common case, and the single most-used screen in the product.
Children without consent are excluded from marking and shown as blocked, not silently missing.
Gated to the class's assigned practitioner.
a: A register is taken once per class per day; late corrections use Edit attendance.
Present/Absent/Late is the full mark vocabulary.
p: Bulk 'mark all absent' for a closed day is proposed, not built.

title: A few things need a look
d: The expanded list behind the Home secondary row. Collects the lower-priority items the Today card suppressed.
dec: Exists so the priority ladder can show one card without hiding the rest of the day's work.
Count badge uses the status-alert tokens, matching the Home row it came from.
a: Ordering mirrors the same priority ladder used for the Today card.
p: No filtering or dismissal here yet; proposed once the list can exceed a screen.

title: Child profile
d: A single child: identity, class, consent state, fee state and the actions available on them.
dec: Consent state is surfaced at the top because it gates everything else.
Actions are role-gated; practitioners without permission see the record but not the edit affordances.
a: One caregiver contact per child in the MVP.
p: Multiple caregivers and a relationship type are proposed.

title: Class detail
d: One class: its children, schedule, and the entry points to take attendance or register a child.
dec: Attendance is the primary action and sits as a full-width primary button.
Child rows show consent state, because consent gates attendance participation.
a: Class size is assumed to fit a single scrolling list; no pagination.
p: Bulk actions across children are proposed, not built.

title: Classes
d: All classes the user can act on, each with its days, times and today's register state.
dec: Practitioners see only their assigned classes; principals see every class in the preschool.
Register state is a badge on the row (To do / Done / No class today) so the day is readable without drilling in.
a: A class has one assigned practitioner at a time; co-teaching is out of scope.
p: Sorting by 'needs attention first' is proposed; today the order is as configured.

title: Coach visit
d: The single-form coach visit record, including GPS capture, completable entirely offline.
dec: One form, no wizard — the coach is standing in a preschool with one hand free.
GPS is captured with the record rather than as a separate check-in.
a: A visit belongs to one preschool and one coach.
p: Photo evidence attached to a visit is proposed.

title: Consent — whole class
d: Consent state for every child in a class, with a bulk send for those outstanding.
dec: Bulk send exists because consent is chased in batches near a deadline.
Children already consented are shown but not selectable, so the list stays a complete picture.
a: Bulk send uses the same per-child template.
p: Staggered sending to avoid message-bundle costs is proposed.

title: Consent received
d: Confirmation that a caregiver's consent has been recorded against a child.
dec: Records who consented and when, because this is the audit trail for a legal obligation.
a: Consent is captured out-of-band and recorded here; the prototype does not model the caregiver's own screen.
p: Attaching the caregiver's signed artefact is proposed.

title: Withdraw consent
d: Records a caregiver withdrawing consent, and the effect that has on the child's participation.
dec: Withdrawal is as easy to record as granting — a compliance requirement, not a symmetry nicety.
The consequence is stated on-screen before confirming.
a: Withdrawal takes effect immediately and blocks attendance marking from that point.
p: A grace period or scheduled withdrawal date is proposed.

title: Deadline warning
d: Warns that a consent deadline is imminent and what happens if it passes.
dec: States the consequence in plain language rather than a date alone.
Uses the design system Alert tokens — orange, not red: this is urgent, not broken.
a: The deadline is a fixed platform-side date.
p: Escalation to the principal when a deadline passes is proposed.

title: Edit attendance
d: Reopens a submitted register so marks can be corrected.
dec: Editing is explicit rather than implicit, so a submitted register is a deliberate record.
Corrections re-enter the sync queue like any other write.
a: Any assigned practitioner may correct the same day's register; no approval step.
p: An edit history / audit trail is proposed for the platform, not shown in the app.

title: Export — configure
d: Choose what to export: date range, class and format.
dec: Range and scope are chosen before generation so a large export is never produced by accident.
a: Only completed periods are offered.
p: Saved export presets are proposed.

title: Export — nothing to export
d: Empty state when the chosen range contains no records.
dec: Offers a way to widen the range instead of a dead end.
a: An empty result is a normal outcome, not an error.
p: Suggesting the nearest range that does contain data is proposed.

title: Export — failed
d: Generation failed, with a retry.
dec: States what to do next rather than surfacing an error code.
Uses the status-error tokens with an icon and a label, never colour alone.
a: Failure is transient and retryable.
p: Reporting a persistent failure to support is proposed.

title: Export — preparing
d: Loading state while the file is generated.
dec: An explicit preparing state rather than a spinner on the button, because generation can take several seconds on low-end devices.
a: Generation is local and does not require connectivity.
p: Background generation with a notification on completion is proposed.

title: Export — queued (offline)
d: The export needs connectivity and has been queued.
dec: Queued rather than blocked — consistent with every other write in the app.
Uses the design system Informational alert, not an error.
a: Queued exports resume automatically on reconnection.
p: A queue view showing everything pending is proposed.

title: Export — ready
d: Success state with the share/open action.
dec: Hands off to the device share sheet rather than an in-app viewer.
a: The device can open the format produced.
p: Recently-generated exports list is proposed.

title: Downloads
d: Registers and reports the user can take away as files.
dec: Exports are a first-class surface because paper records are still required by funders and the DBE.
a: Exports are generated on the device from local data.
p: Emailing an export directly is proposed.

title: Home — Today
d: The daily landing screen. A navy hero carries the greeting and date; below it a single Today card states the one thing that matters now, then the 'a few things need a look' row, then the resource-category shortcuts.
dec: Exactly one Today card at a time, chosen by a priority ladder (consent-imminent → attendance-due → month-start). Competing nudges are suppressed, not stacked.
Built as the design system's Action Panel 'with link' (Figma 100:7530), the slot Figma's hub notification frame (145:27122) reserves above the category list.
Shortcut labels are the Resources taxonomy verbatim, so Home and Resources cannot drift.
a: 'Good morning/afternoon/evening' is derived from device time, not from server time.
The greeting uses the practitioner's first name only; long names are untested beyond ~18 characters.
p: Hub notifications carry a priority number so only one shows — the priority table is referenced in the use-case doc but not yet encoded here.
Consider a dismiss affordance on the Today card; today it clears only when the underlying task is done.

title: Identity document
d: The scaffolded identity step: seven document types, a real SA-ID checksum, and a derived date of birth.
dec: Validates the SA ID checksum client-side so errors surface before submission, offline.
Date of birth is derived from the ID rather than asked twice.
Deferrable — 'Do this later' is a supported path, not a dead end.
a: Seven document types cover the population; a fallback 'other' is not offered.
Closed-tenant mismatch is gated for SmartStart only.
p: Photographing the document is proposed; today it is keyed in.

title: Income
d: The month's money position: collected so far, and the entry points to the paid checklist and expenses.
dec: Principal-only, reached from the principal bottom nav.
Leads with the collected figure because that is the question being asked.
a: One fee cycle per month.
p: Multi-cycle and per-child schedules are proposed.

title: Mark a child as left
d: Records that a child has left the programme, with a reason and optional note.
dec: A leave is a state change on the record, never a delete — the register history must stay intact.
Reason is a closed list so the data is analysable.
a: Leaving is reversible by an administrator; the prototype does not show that path.
p: A 'returned' state is proposed for seasonal attendance.

title: Menu (drawer)
d: Full-height drawer opened from the hamburger. Role-scoped list of destinations that do not warrant a bottom-nav slot.
dec: Overflow lives in a drawer rather than a fifth nav tab, keeping the bottom nav at four items for practitioners.
Rows use the design system 48 dp list-row with a leading duotone icon.
a: Drawer contents are the same for both tenants; only branding changes.
p: Menu order is not yet personalised by frequency of use.

title: Month summary
d: Income against expenses for the month, and the resulting position.
dec: Outcome is colour-coded with the status tokens — success for a surplus, error for a shortfall — never colour alone, always with the figure.
a: The month is the reporting unit.
p: Year-to-date and trend are proposed.

title: Notification settings
d: Per-category toggles controlling which notifications the user receives.
dec: Defaults are opt-in for operational alerts (attendance, consent) and opt-out for digests.
a: Channel choice (push vs SMS) is assumed to be a platform setting, not exposed here.
p: Quiet hours are proposed; not in the MVP.

title: Notifications
d: Chronological list of system notifications, with unread state driving the header bell badge.
dec: Unread count is computed from the local store so the badge is correct offline.
Tapping a notification routes to the underlying record rather than opening a detail view of the notification itself.
a: Notifications are generated client-side in the prototype; production will receive them from the platform.
p: Grouping by day and a 'mark all read' action are proposed but not built.

title: Payment saved
d: Confirmation after recording payments, with sync state.
dec: Same save-and-sync language as attendance, so money and register behave identically offline.
a: Payments queue offline like any other write.
p: A printable/ shareable receipt is proposed.

title: Profile
d: The user's own record: identity, preschool, network, and the completion prompt if the identity step was deferred.
dec: Deferred onboarding surfaces here as 'Complete your profile' rather than blocking use of the app.
The prompt is a design system Action Panel, matching the Home Today card's shape.
a: One preschool per user in the MVP.
p: Switching between preschools is stubbed and proposed.

title: Register a child
d: Minimum-plus-scaffold registration: the few fields needed to enrol, with the rest deferrable.
dec: Only the fields required to take a register are mandatory; everything else can be completed later, matching the onboarding identity step.
Incomplete records save with a visible flag rather than blocking enrolment.
a: A child can be enrolled before consent is received; consent is chased separately.
p: Self-registration by caregivers via a share link exists as a parallel path (see Self-registration).

title: Register status
d: Whether each class's register is done for the day, across the classes the user can see.
dec: Principal-oriented overview that answers 'is the day covered?' without opening each class.
a: Only today is shown; historical coverage lives in exports.
p: A week view is proposed.

title: Remove staff
d: Removes a staff member, with the class-coverage consequence stated first.
dec: Blocks or warns when removal would leave a class uncovered — the flow's whole purpose is that every class keeps a practitioner.
a: Removal is not a delete; historical registers keep their author.
p: A scheduled last-day is proposed rather than immediate removal.

title: Resource category — Early learning activities
d: The resources inside one category: title, a one-line description, and whether opening it will use the user's data.
dec: The data-free flag is stated on every item, because data cost is a real barrier for this audience.
Reached identically from Home and from Resources — one destination, two entry points.
Items are presentational in this build; the app has no in-app resource viewer.
a: The data-free flag is set per resource on the platform, not inferred.
Resources open outside the app in the browser.
p: An 'opens outside the app and uses data' confirmation dialog exists in the wider resources module and is proposed for this build.
Offline caching of data-free documents is proposed.

title: Resources
d: The four resource categories: Running your preschool, Early learning activities, Health and safety, Funding and subsidies.
dec: This list is the single source of truth for the resource taxonomy — the Home shortcuts mirror it exactly.
Category-first rather than search-first, because the library is small and browsing beats querying at this size.
a: Four categories are sufficient for the MVP library.
p: Search across categories exists in the wider resources module but is not surfaced in this build.

title: Self-registration — share link
d: Generates a link a caregiver can use to register their own child, removing typing from the practitioner.
dec: Sharing uses the device share sheet so it works with WhatsApp, the dominant channel for this audience.
The link is scoped to one class.
a: Links do not expire in the prototype.
p: Expiry and single-use links are proposed for production.

title: Self-registration — status
d: Which caregivers have completed the self-registration form and which are outstanding.
dec: Completion is visible per child so chasing is targeted rather than broadcast.
a: A submission maps to exactly one child.
p: Reminder nudges from this screen are proposed.

title: Send consent request
d: Sends a consent request to a child's caregiver.
dec: Consent is treated as a first-class, time-bound obligation rather than a profile field.
The send action queues offline and reports that it will send on reconnection.
a: One consent request per child at a time; re-sending replaces the outstanding request.
p: Templated multilingual consent copy is proposed.

title: Request sent
d: Confirmation that a consent request has left the device or been queued.
dec: Distinguishes 'sent' from 'queued' so the user is never misled while offline.
a: Delivery receipts are not modelled.
p: Delivery and read state from the messaging channel is proposed.

title: Set fees
d: Sets the class fee that auto-populates each child's monthly amount.
dec: Fee is set at class level and overridable per child, so the common case is one number.
Auto-populated values remain editable — the review explicitly kept this.
a: Fee changes apply from the current month forward, not retroactively.
p: Sibling discounts and bursaries are proposed.

title: Preschool details
d: The preschool's own record — name, address and identifying details.
dec: Read-oriented; editing is deliberately narrow because these fields feed platform registration.
a: One site per preschool.
p: Multi-site organisations are proposed, out of MVP scope.

title: Staff member
d: One staff member: their classes and the leave/reassign actions.
dec: Class coverage is shown next to the person, so the consequence of marking leave is visible before acting.
a: A practitioner can hold multiple classes.
p: Contact details and qualifications are proposed for a later release.

title: Staff
d: Everyone at the preschool, their classes, and who is currently on leave.
dec: Principal-only surface, reached from the principal's bottom nav.
Leave state is on the row because it changes who can take a register.
a: Staff are practitioners or the principal; no other roles in the MVP.
p: Assistant and volunteer roles were considered and explicitly cut.

title: Staff removed
d: Confirmation, including where the removed member's classes went.
dec: Names the reassignment explicitly so coverage is auditable.
a: Reassignment is chosen during removal, not after.
p: Undo within a session is proposed.

title: Who's paid?
d: A monthly checklist of every child's fee state, with part-payment capture.
dec: A checklist rather than a ledger — the principal is reconciling against cash in hand, not doing bookkeeping.
Part payments are first-class: the row shows paid-of-owed and the balance.
Status pills use the platform status tokens, so Paid/Part/Not paid read the same as every other state in the app.
a: Fees are per-child per-month and auto-populated from the class fee.
Cash is the dominant channel; no reconciliation against a bank feed.
p: Receipts to caregivers are proposed, not built.
Arrears carried across months are proposed.

dec: Phone number and a one-time code — no passwords, no SSO. A wrong code is retriable and nothing locks.
Every step that can be deferred is deferrable; deferral surfaces later as 'Complete your profile'.
a: The OTP is a fixed code in the prototype (123456).
p: Copy is placeholder in places and pending a plain-language pass.
